approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from scored survivors, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process and a frozen native tabular quantile model to the current session’s accepted scores, and buys sequential sampled maxima. It uses the Gaussian-process mean for eligibility and location, while translated native quantiles supply the residual spread, asymmetry and bounded tails. A standardized draw from the original Gaussian-process factor supplies dependence. Its stall rule restricts eligibility to the forty highest means after three stalled batches.
approach.novelty: Replace only the centered native residual shape by a Gaussian with exactly the native integrated variance. This tests whether bounded tails and other non-Gaussian shape hinder productive purchases once Gaussian-process location is restored. The Parent changed location; the earlier coordinate-adapter variant changed native inputs. Neither isolated shape at fixed location and variance, and the brief contains no completed children of this Parent. No amplitude multiplier or feature adapter is added.

observed_bottleneck: On code Parent n-e2506e11f536, complete GP-location translation raises full positive score-minus-best-actual-generating-parent gain to 14.212983699997896 from 11.189064122623599 in n-16b934239c55, but late gain falls to 4.445967758637079 from 4.943625601057764. Mean endpoint 0.5589888753493724 (population seed SD 0.02055446360783425) remains 0.04804144086175869 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. Native residual scale and bounded/asymmetric shape are still inseparable: on the Parent paid stream, central-90% width is 0.17782235585517736 versus passive GP 0.09878172042737944, while native-residual pinball 0.02023840351299787 is better than GP 0.022170072530832197. Thus neither narrower uncertainty nor improved calibration is established as the remedy. The testable bottleneck is whether the retained non-Gaussian residual shape limits productive selection at fixed native variance; it is a hypothesis, not established causation. Evidence is the Parent’s all-three-seed summaries/run logs, archived analysis and hash-matched per-cell paid/generating-parent audits, with n-16b934239c55 as its actual predecessor and n-cf8d309c06de separately as formal Anchor.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already supplies complete finite monotone quantiles and exact integrated means on its current-session count inputs. Moment integration applies to that defined spline; its variance is predictive and need not be calibrated noiseless utility. The Parent’s remaining residual obstacle motivates the campaign intervention.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Quantile integration separates the learned conditional marginal’s mean and centered variance from its higher-order shape.

deviations.adopted_setting: The existing molecular Parent’s 999-knot constant-tail spline defines m and v; only the active standardized residual shape is projected to an unbounded Gaussian at the inherited GP location and native v.
deviations.paper_setting: TabICLv2 native regression quantile distributions, including the paper’s full exponential-tail construction.
deviations.reason: This is the frozen variance-matched shape intervention on an implemented host, not a paper algorithm, a source-validated molecular method or a claim of better calibration. Native tails enter the variance integral but are intentionally absent from the active law.

adoptions.implementation_change: Retain NativeQuantiles.fit/predict and the existing frozen source/checkpoint/native preprocessing. In the select consumer helper integrate (Q-m)^2 directly over inherited KNOTS including both constant tails; use that variance in the Gaussianized residual, without new model inference or variance fitting.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already records all dependence arrays and supplies both marginal moments and GP location. Retaining latent Gaussian dependence permits a single marginal-shape replacement; it does not preserve output Pearson covariance under changing nonlinear marginals or establish a calibrated posterior over utility.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Separate a Gaussian dependence construction from the marginal inverse-CDF consumer.

deviations.adopted_setting: Use the existing molecular count-GP standardized joint draw with a Gaussian marginal matched to each native constant-tail variance, fixed GP mean and unchanged paid sampled-maxima consumer.
deviations.paper_setting: Copula-process construction permits different marginal inverse CDFs under Gaussian dependence.
deviations.reason: This campaign adaptation isolates the registered residual-shape question. Direct use of z avoids inverse-normal rounding at diagnostic uniforms 0/1, draws no new randomness and makes no source claim of optimization gain.

adoptions.implementation_change: Reuse the original actual jittered GP factor and original normal stream to obtain standardized z and diagnostic Phi(z). In FingerprintPosterior.select consume mu_GP+sqrt(v_native)*z; retain the old translated inverse quantile on the same u only as passive Parent replay.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review and its recorded original queries/retrieval artifacts; no new search is claimed. Carry the portfolio-position-2 mixed adoption exactly: native centered moment integration plus separation of marginal shape from latent copula, with the Gaussian projection a campaign intervention. Complete GP-location evidence supports this testable residual question, while better native pinball and the negative original complete recipe remain contrary evidence. Neither source validates productive purchases, calibration, latent utility, raw-covariance preservation or Anchor attainment.

sources.applicability: Retain the pinned model. Integrate the already registered constant-tail spline, not the paper exponential tails. Shape and scale controls below are campaign interventions, not source-validated molecular methods.
sources.finding: Conditional quantile distributions expose location, variance and non-Gaussian shape through quantile integration.
sources.title: TabICLv2 — Qu et al., v2, Appendix I

sources.applicability: Retain the same standardized Gaussian draws while changing one marginal consumer. Latent copula preservation is not preservation of Pearson covariance after nonlinear transport, nor latent-utility calibration.
sources.finding: A Gaussian dependence construction can be transported through different marginal inverse CDFs.
sources.title: Copula Processes — Wilson and Ghahramani, NeurIPS 2010

hypothesis: Variance-preserving Gaussianization of only the native centered residual marginal: for inherited constant-tail piecewise-linear Q_i, inherited exact integrated mean m_i, and directly integrated v_i = integral_0^1 (Q_i(u)-m_i)^2 du, consume S_ri = mu_GP_i + sqrt(v_i) z_ri, where z = (original_normals @ original_jittered_factor.T)/actual_factor_row_norms. Retain the original GP mean/mask, native feature filtering and model fitting, native marginal variance, actual factor, original normal stream and sequential first-index sampled maxima. Gaussianization jointly replaces bounded tails, asymmetry and higher moments; it preserves latent Gaussian dependence, not raw Pearson covariance. Exactly zero v_i consumes mu_GP_i exactly. The claimed path is shape change, changed actual purchases, real next-fit/breeding exposure, then increased complete generating-parent gain; score is a separate outcome.

finding_summary.headline: Gaussian residuals raise generating-parent gain, but mean final score falls and the Anchor target remains unmet
finding_summary.insights: The residual-shape change operated and increased the preregistered total of offspring improvements, but that quantity did not deliver a better final incumbent. The gain surplus is driven by one seed and is largest in DRD2 docking, while the strongest endpoint loss is in sitagliptin MPO. These data settle the stated aggregate useful-shape test positively; they do not establish reliable score benefit, superiority of native variance over GP variance, or benefit from removing any single feature of the native shape, because bounded tails, asymmetry and higher moments changed together. Both literature-derived elements operated: exact quantile moment integration and reuse of Gaussian dependence. The constant-tail spline and Gaussian projection remain campaign adaptations, so the result does not inherit literature claims of calibration or molecular optimization performance. The molecular assessment shows broad pooled graph coverage alongside only 1–9 typed cores in each session’s highest-scoring ten molecules. Moreover, 3,432 of 4,350 purchases scored below their actual generating parents. This is evidence of uneven productive core exploration and weak conversion of local offspring gains into better endpoints; it does not identify residual shape as the only bottleneck. A proposal operator or search scheme that can reorganize core connectivity while retaining useful local chemistry could address that limitation. The visible chemical motifs and score ties do not establish a particular missing pharmacophore or a causal chemical explanation for the endpoint loss. Scale, input visibility, ranking quality and their interactions remain open, as does transfer beyond this three-seed Search panel.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches ran correctly, preserving the GP location, native marginal variance and original normal stream. Gaussian residuals changed the selected set in 427 batches, creating 1,464 purchases absent from the same-state native-shape replay. All 1,400 of these purchases with a next-fit opportunity entered both real models; the final 64 were right-censored. Positive score gain over actual generating parents rose from 14.21298 to 15.09538 across 4,350 purchases, and from 4.44597 to 5.38387 across the 2,175 late purchases. This passes the registered scientific criterion. The aggregate gain increase is uneven: two seed totals decreased and the third increased; the middle phase and restricted-mask strata also lost gain. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.55899 to 0.53979, a paired change of -0.01919, and was 0.06724 below the formal Anchor. The required 0.60903 mean was not attained. Same-label mean pinball loss was nearly unchanged by shape alone (0.017774 Gaussian versus 0.017826 translated native), while 90% coverage rose from 78.67% to 81.08%. Mean ordering was exactly equal on those common states, as required by the shared GP mean.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles, fluorinated carbonyl cores and amine-rich polycycles; unusual attachments and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: For n-a03f82e62383, the complete supplied Search panel contains 4350 accepted optimizer molecules, excluding 150 initial records. All fifteen Child and fifteen published code-Parent n-e2506e11f536 trajectories were read. The frozen comparison separately records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0, 1 and 2; no listed trajectory is missing. These are accepted proposals, not the unobserved full candidate pools or rejected submissions. Child paths are the exact request-trusted staging paths outside runs/SPIRAL2; they are not archived run-relative evidence. Parent paths are published and authoritative. The separate input manifest, per-cell audit-seed files and citation receipt under policy/scratch/r0064-01-improve-L01 retain paths, hashes, seeds, tasks and citation locations; no archive paths were fabricated. The molecules combine recognizable amides, ketones, cyclic carbonyl systems, ethers, heteroaromatics and amines with less conventional N-halogen/O-halogen attachments and congested fused or small rings. RDKit readings of the accepted optimizer stream give a median of 30 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and three aromatic rings; size spans 1 to 120 heavy atoms. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9966 to 1.0 and aromatic-token rates 0.992 to 0.9977, consistent with rich ring/aromatic content rather than acyclic collapse. There are 1963 distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1265 generic scaffolds, but individual highest-score ten-molecule cohorts contain only 1 to 9 typed cores. This is moderate effective diversity: many graph variants coexist with local core concentration. All 4350 optimizer structures are connected and have no formally charged atom or assigned perceived tetrahedral centre; 2378 contain at least one unassigned perceived centre. This does not establish their solution charge or absence of stereochemistry. N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bonds occur in 809, 179 and 76 molecules, versus 704, 161 and 71 for the Parent; these overlapping motif flags are not measured instability or toxicity. Carbon-allene-bearing structures fall from 119 in the Parent to 9 here, so the chemistry change is mixed. The small and large size tails are 5 molecules at <=6 heavy atoms and 423 at >=60, versus Parent 23 and 384. Nonempty-scaffold counting excludes the empty acyclic scaffold; this explains why this Parent reading is 1950 rather than a count that includes the empty scaffold. Synthetic plausibility is a structural judgement, not a route assessment: ordinary substructures occur, yet N-halogen motifs, amino-substituted small rings, complex fused connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry make many complete products questionable. Drug-likeness is moderate by appearance only; no synthesis, physical stability, solubility, potency or safety was measured here. All chemical/score associations below are conditional on this Search panel, without mechanism activation or component-attribution claims.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted proposals are mostly compact fused nitrogen heteroaromatics with an aryl amide or aryl-linked ketone, methoxy/alkyl groups and frequent halogens. The heavy-atom median is 25 (range 10..48), with median three rings and three aromatic rings; none reaches either <=6 or >=60 heavy atoms. The seed-0 best has 25 heavy atoms and combines an N-fluoro anilide with an N-amino fused ring. Seed 1 instead finds an indole-like aryl ketone carrying a fluorinated azaaryl substituent; seed 2 finds an annulated N-heterocycle with a benzyl ketone. These are distinguishable chemical families, but the seed-0 highest ten all share one typed Murcko core. The late seed-2 examples retain related fused cores rather than indicating ring loss. Compared with the Parent, the median size changes from 24 to 25 heavy atoms and N-halogen-bearing structures from 87 to 275; both panels retain compact aryl-carbonyl heterocycles.
liabilities: Frequent N-halogen attachment, plus N-amino/N-sulfur substitutions, weakens confidence in stability and makeability despite valid molecular graphs.
Large early coupled ring systems score extremely poorly; peripheral variants can preserve a core and score without supplying a distinct productive core family.
missing_features: Consistently accessible compact alternatives with ordinary N-substitution are underrepresented in the seed-0 high-score family; other seeds show that an N-halogen bond is not necessary for every relatively high observed score.

The trajectories do not identify a uniquely missing target pharmacophore. Configuration and chemically meaningful charge alternatives remain unspecified when applicable; no score benefit for adding them is demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The Child seed maxima are 0.46092619585962435, 0.42762099872850584 and 0.43351949803907636, with compact 23..25-heavy-atom cores. The large coupled heteroaromatic example in cited_smiles scores 3.3264465583049668e-15. The observations associate useful scores with compact substituted fused cores, rather than indiscriminate duplication of those cores; they do not isolate which atom edit helps. The equally scoring methoxy/alkyl N-sulfur variant at 0.4394278959350887 shows that a high score is compatible with questionable attachment chemistry. Parent seed maxima are 0.44989726212142783, 0.4454539912731944 and 0.43554057891621306: the visible changes do not establish a uniform chemical improvement.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most heterogeneous output: median 50 heavy atoms, range 4..120, with median 7.5 perceived rings and six aromatic rings. There are 371 of 870 proposals at >=60 heavy atoms, including 187 of 435 late proposals. Seed 0 elaborates very large linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies; its best has 86 heavy atoms and ten aromatic rings. Seed 1 instead produces compact O,N-containing carbonyl heterocycles with a fused cyclic ether and linked pyridyl rings: its best has 28 heavy atoms and five rings. Seed 2 retains a nitrogen-rich multiheteroaromatic carbonyl assembly with N-bromo and nitroso attachments. The Parent already spans tiny fragments to 120-heavy-atom molecules; its median is 42.5 and its >=60 tail contains 346 proposals. The Child therefore does not solve the large-assembly tendency, although its strongest observed seed-1 family is compact.
liabilities: The many very large, polyaromatic and heavily carbonylated assemblies raise practical synthesis and physicochemical questions that the score does not answer.
N-bromo, nitroso and occasional peroxide-like O-O linkages occur; they warrant separate chemical assessment, not an assumption that score measures developability.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, coherent ring/linker alternatives is uneven across seeds: one productive family exists while other sessions persist with large linked assemblies.

No specific absent functional group can be identified as the objective requirement from these trajectories. The missing capability is broader productive core reorganization without obligatory whole-core duplication.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact seed-1 fused ether/heteroaryl carbonyl molecule scores 0.6610996157256873; replacing a peripheral methyl with chlorine gives the same supplied score. The seed-0 large assembly reaches 0.6000417929161007 and the seed-2 N-bromo/nitroso assembly 0.5984722510912492. Oxetane scores 0.5, while a small chlorofluorophenol scores 0.5052914719111032. Thus organized ring/linker context matters in the observed associations, and higher scores do not require the largest molecules; simple fragmentation also fails to reproduce the higher scores. The Parent seed maxima are 0.60808124728244, 0.6284615865474776 and 0.5982257793697878. Cross-seed size differences are not a matched substitution test or a universal size rule.

per_task.generated_character: The typical proposal has 32 heavy atoms, five rings and two aromatic rings, with a full size range of 13..112 heavy atoms. Higher-score structures combine halogenated aromatic regions with available aliphatic amines, sometimes in fused/polycyclic frameworks. Seed 1 gives a 32-heavy-atom polycycle carrying an N-propyl pyrrolidine, a ketone and an amino-substituted N-methyl aziridine. Seed 2 instead reaches a high score with a flexible 30-heavy-atom bis-aryl framework and several acyclic amines/aminal-like links; seed 0 retains amines around a more unsaturated polycyclic framework. The Parent also produces amine-rich halogenated polycycles. The Child has fewer typical rings (median five in both, mean 4.64 versus 5.20), but more O-halogen-bearing proposals: 136 versus 17. Thirty-seven proposals have >=60 heavy atoms, falling to two in the late cohort.
liabilities: The seed-1 best includes an amino-substituted aziridine and several unspecified stereogenic environments; graph validity does not establish its stability or a feasible route.
A large aromatic/halogen burden, O-halogen attachments and some aminal-like chains make chemical robustness and physicochemical behaviour uncertain.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical alternatives are absent despite 802 of 870 proposals containing an unassigned perceived tetrahedral centre; ionization alternatives are also unrepresented in the supplied neutral graphs.

The higher-score molecules already contain aliphatic amine centres, so their absence is not a supported gap. Ordinary local-bonding alternatives around those centres, without strained amino-small-rings or aminal-like links, are not consistently represented among the illustrated endpoints.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The Child seed maxima are 0.8807783738548965, 0.9999927209662445 and 0.9891310964263093. The 0.9999927209662445 molecule combines accessible aliphatic nitrogens and a rigid hydrophobic/aromatic framework, whereas the small N-chloro amide attached to an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00016650955053713697 and related chlorophenyl sulfonyl fragments are also low. The visible gradient is consistent with retaining amine-bearing aromatic context rather than isolated sulfonyl fragments; basicity is inferred structurally, not measured. The flexible seed-2 amine-rich best shows that a fused cage is not necessary for all high scores. Parent seed maxima of 0.9401808180557334, 0.994627130457666 and 0.8420875941513817 describe mixed changes. No receptor interaction, pose quality, experimental affinity or clinical activity follows from these scalar values.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 34 heavy atoms, five rings and three aromatic rings, spanning 1..81 heavy atoms. Higher-score families join alkyl/ethoxy-substituted aryl or azaaryl groups to polycyclic nitrogen-rich lactam/urea-like carbonyl systems. The seed-2 best is a 31-heavy-atom quinoline-linked, partially saturated nitrogen/carbonyl ring assembly; seed 1 uses two aromatic regions around a fused carbonyl/N-N-containing core, and seed 0 uses a larger substituted nitrogen-rich polycycle. The final seed-2 proposals remain close variants of this core. Four proposals have <=6 heavy atoms and fifteen >=60. The Parent median is 32 heavy atoms, with related azaaryl and N-methyl carbonyl rings; its smaller and larger tails contain fourteen and nine proposals respectively. This is not a ring-deficient search.
liabilities: N-N/N-O-containing and densely fused nitrogen-rich cores complicate chemical interpretation and synthesis; their presence is not by itself evidence of instability.
Occasional trivial fragments and large core duplications spend accepted evaluations outside the compact-to-medium higher-score families.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent exploration of chemically simpler alternative connections between its aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl regions while retaining the features associated with higher observed scores.
There is no evidence here for a missing named target scaffold. Specified configurations are absent even though 419 proposals contain perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329; Child seed maxima are 0.22219032811050834, 0.22726273704316693 and 0.2301832555365978. Methane and acetylene score 0, hexylamine 0.01877017411450683 and cyclopentane 0.027826129037656074. The visible associations favour preserving the extended aromatic plus nitrogen/carbonyl topology rather than reducing it to simple fragments. Late close analogues remain around the best region, with the cited final example scoring 0.2213243509858485, but this does not reveal a uniquely optimal arrangement. Parent seed maxima are 0.2363146341487732, 0.22344648696506328 and 0.2121823339838681; the best-scoring Parent example is not surpassed by a simple universal increase in size.

per_task.generated_character: These are medium-sized, fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles: median 27 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings, spanning 18..57 heavy atoms. No proposal occupies either <=6 or >=60 tail. The seed-2 best has a fused N-methyl/N-fluoro carbonyl core, a fluorinated unsaturated carbocycle, fluoroalkyl groups and an oxime-like side chain. Seed 1 couples a similar carbonyl core to small fused unsaturated rings; seed 0 uses a partially saturated carbonyl framework with a dihydroxyphenyl group. N-halogen bonds occur in 408 of 870 proposals and unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres in 688. The Parent already shows fluorinated carbonyl/imino and fused-ring chemistry, with median 28 heavy atoms; its N-halogen count is 416. The Child has far fewer carbon-allene-bearing molecules, five versus 108, without a uniform improvement in supplied endpoints.
liabilities: N-fluoro carbonyl nitrogens, heavily substituted small unsaturated rings and oxime-like branches make chemical robustness and synthetic access uncertain.
Similarity in visible motifs does not protect against extremely low scores; additional ring/atom edits should not be presumed chemically or objectively beneficial.
missing_features: The trajectories do not reveal a required absent target motif; fluorine, carbonyls and ring complexity are already abundant. The unsupported part is reliable navigation among ordinary attachment environments and close whole-molecule compositions while retaining the observed useful family.
Configuration and oxime/alkene geometry are unspecified in the illustrated high-score structures; no evidence establishes which configuration, if any, would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The Child seed maxima are 0.3689433490219305, 0.4602706036821303 and 0.5364835778525856. The 27-heavy-atom seed-2 best scores 0.5364835778525856, compared with 1.2669702988079034e-48 for the large coupled carbonyl/aryl assembly in cited_smiles. The initial aromatic carbonyl compound scores only 0.0020944534688323298. The observed gradient favours a constrained medium-size, fluorinated carbonyl/heterocycle region over large duplicated aromatic assemblies. It is sharply sensitive within that region: the final small-ring hydroxylated analogue scores 0.0002983034893201377 despite retaining many of the same conspicuous motifs. This is not an isolated substitution pair and does not establish which objective component causes the change. Parent seed maxima are 0.506913769157628, 0.6467462742507727 and 0.6166736435591553; fewer allene flags therefore cannot be treated as a score explanation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-a03f82e62383 accepted optimizer trajectories in the frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared with published code Parent n-e2506e11f536 under the same profile and budget. N-halogen-bearing molecules number 809 versus 704, O-halogen-bearing molecules 179 versus 161, and O-O-bearing molecules 76 versus 71. High-score examples retain N-fluoro carbonyl nitrogens, N-amino ring atoms or amino-substituted small rings. Carbon-allene exposure moves in the opposite direction, 9 versus 119. These are overlapping structure flags and conditional chemistry associations, not stability measurements or component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably vary useful cores while preserving ordinary local attachment chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic editing capability would need to offer ordinary attachment alternatives around retained ring, carbonyl and amine arrangements, distinguishing the attachment atom from the whole-core identity. Use only current-session observations to learn which alternatives help; these findings do not justify a universal motif ban or assert that structural cleanup raises scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the same complete n-a03f82e62383 Search panel. No accepted optimizer molecule has an assigned perceived tetrahedral centre or a formally charged atom, although 2378 of 4350 contain an unassigned perceived centre. High-score examples include polycyclic amines, amino-small-rings and fluorinated partially saturated carbonyl cores. The Parent likewise has no assigned centre or charged atom, with 2574 molecules containing unassigned centres. Neutral input graphs do not determine solution protonation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not express configuration and ionization alternatives for the stereogenic and potentially ionizable molecules it generates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general representation and generator would need to preserve or propose chemically meaningful configurations and charge alternatives when applicable, without changing canonical identity rules or using target identity. This is missing representational coverage, not evidence that any particular stereoisomer or protonation state improves the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-a03f82e62383 and the paired published Parent Search trajectories. The Child has 5 optimizer proposals with <=6 heavy atoms and 423 with >=60, versus Parent 23 and 384; its overall median is 30 and maximum 120. Some higher-score families are compact connected heterocycles, whereas one session retains a large linked polyheteroaromatic family even late. Tiny standalone fragments also occur and can score poorly. All accepted optimizer structures are connected, so this is not a disconnected-component finding.
transferable_gaps.gap: Access to useful ring and linker arrangements is uneven across both size tails and across sessions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General graph edits would need to preserve coherent functional-group and linker relationships during both contraction and elaboration, while maintaining access to different core sizes. Keep both tails observable and let local scores decide survival. These data do not support a universal heavy-atom floor, ceiling, fragment reward or size penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-a03f82e62383 on the complete frozen Search panel. The accepted stream has 1963 nonempty typed Murcko cores and 1265 generic cores, but its fifteen separate highest-score ten-molecule cohorts contain only 1 to 9 typed cores each. Exact score ties occur among peripheral substitutions on the same core. The Parent has 1950 nonempty typed cores and 1304 generic cores under the same audit convention. Broad pooled graph variety therefore coexists with local core concentration; scaffold counts alone are not a diversity benefit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct graphs do not consistently provide several substantially different productive core families within a session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need continued access to changes in core connectivity and ring geometry as well as peripheral analogues, preserving ordinary chemistry during those changes. Treat scaffold coverage as a conditional diagnostic, not an auxiliary objective, known-answer scaffold list or proof that a search component caused an endpoint difference.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Original current-session raw-score count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto GP location, normalization, covariance and original Gaussian factor/normal stream.
